_comment: Comparison fleet. Same provenance discipline as rolling_stock.json:
published / derived / modelled / unknown
WHERE THE GAPS ARE, stated up front so no plot silently hides one:
* N700S formation mass is published only as an UPPER BOUND ('under 700 t').
It is carried as a bound, and any quantity derived from it is a one-sided
bound too -- power-to-weight for the N700S is a MINIMUM, not a value.
* Service deceleration is not captured for the E5 or the N700S.
* The E233 deceleration figure was published without a service/emergency
qualifier. See the note on that entry.
AERODYNAMICS -- the biggest cross-class modelling hazard:
The Davis estimator in resistance.py was built for a blunt-nosed commuter
EMU. Applying it unchanged to a Shinkansen would be wrong by a large
factor: a 15 m streamlined nose has a fraction of the pressure drag, while
400 m of train body has far more skin friction. Per-class aero parameters
are given below, but the Shinkansen values are estimates with much weaker
grounding than the commuter ones, and TUNNEL AERODYNAMICS ARE NOT MODELLED
AT ALL -- which is a first-order omission on the Tokaido. Treat any
Shinkansen running-resistance number here as indicative only.
The three comparison axes the project actually reports (acceleration vs
maximum speed, power-to-weight, braking distance) depend on running
resistance either not at all or only weakly, so the headline comparison is
not compromised by this. Anything else derived from these coefficients is.

service_deceleration_kmh_s.warning: Published as 減速度 5.0 km/h/s with no service/emergency qualifier captured. For this class the maximum SERVICE rate is normally quoted lower than the emergency rate, so 5.0 is more likely the emergency figure. Braking comparisons involving the E233 should be read with that in mind rather than treated as like-for-like against the E235's explicitly-service 4.2.

service_deceleration_kmh_s.note: Not captured from the sources consulted. Excluded from braking comparisons rather than filled with a peer value.
